description: RA-02 defense in depth for in-process role assumption. When a process runs with SYSTEM_ROLE (surface_runtime launches every surface with SYSTEM_ROLE=<surface id>; `pnpm surfaces` and `pnpm config-mission` set it for their own runtimes), withExecutionContext / withExecutionContextAsync may only assume the SYSTEM_ROLE itself, the shared core roles, or the roles listed for that system role here; anything else throws [ROLE_ASSUMPTION_DENIED]. A SYSTEM_ROLE without an entry may only assume itself. Processes without SYSTEM_ROLE are unaffected. Lists are derived from static reachability of withExecutionContext call sites (literal role arguments and the governed-artifact role wrappers) from each surface entry point; see knowledge/product/governance/AUTHORITY_MODEL.md section 3.B2.

shared_core_roles.rationale: Roles that libs/core modules assume internally on behalf of every caller and that every surface reaches through @agent/core: mission_controller (mission lifecycle, dispatch, task grants, agent identity, plugin approvals, provider egress), sovereign_concierge (authn principal registry, tool runtime policy, onboarding), infrastructure_sentinel (work coordination, peer messaging, mesh), ecosystem_architect (storage janitor, background review), knowledge_steward (mission creation), and the GovernedArtifactRole set of artifact-store / surface stores (chronos_gateway, slack_bridge, surface_runtime).

chronos_mirror_v2.rationale: Chronos viewer-scoped routes assume chronos_localadmin / chronos_operator (withViewerExecutionContext*, plugin-host-boot tenant registry reads, plugin approvals); the generation scheduler module reached from Chronos assumes generation_scheduler.

computer_surface.rationale: presence/displays/computer-surface/server.ts assumes ecosystem_architect only (a shared core role).

concierge.rationale: Concierge routes assume sovereign_concierge (shared) and the viewer-scoped concierge_localadmin / concierge_operator roles (withConciergeViewerContext).

mcp_server_cowork.rationale: scripts/mcp_server.ts reaches only shared core roles (cowork-surface assumes surface_runtime).

presence_studio.rationale: Presence Studio routes assume ecosystem_architect, sovereign_concierge and mission_controller (all shared).

surface_runtime.rationale: `pnpm surfaces` and the terminal HUD run scripts/surface_runtime.ts with SYSTEM_ROLE=surface_runtime; it reaches only shared core roles.

system_configurator.rationale: `pnpm config-mission` and its preset pipeline child (scripts/config_mission.ts) run with SYSTEM_ROLE=system_configurator; they reach only shared core roles.
